name: Gadelhak v. AT&T Services, Inc.
summary: The Seventh Circuit held that certain statutory violations involving unwanted communications constituted concrete injuries sufficient for Article III standing based on their close analogy to historically recognized common law harms.
significance: This Seventh Circuit decision, among others from sister circuits, is cited to illustrate the circuit split on whether bare statutory privacy violations confer standing — a split the Supreme Court granted certiorari to resolve.
